event.summary: Restart retention no longer rejects listings started before the reply
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: a successful Restart might lose its temporary terminal-presence override before the session listing catches up, leaving an interrupted card where a running terminal should be. Source basis: the assigned patch removes the listing-generation argument and the test assertion that an already-in-flight running listing must not retire a Restart (old lines 4625–4650; new 4484–4497). Checks made: complete assigned session_view patch read. Missing premise: whether shipped callers still fence old listing responses, and whether any accepted response can retire success while a newly opened view receives stale Interrupted state. Next: inspect pinned SessionOps and list/detail callers with governing specifications; no runtime reproduction requested. Suggested bucket: high/material UX if established; could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work or security route. Confidence: uninvestigated lead. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveat: retention implementation is adjacent-group code and may independently fence this sequence.

event.summary: A delayed pre-Restart stale listing can suppress terminal remount after success
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: after reconnecting to a host and successfully restarting an interrupted session, the view can continue showing the interrupted card until a later detail refresh succeeds, even though its agent is running. Suggested bucket: other (temporary attachment/presentation failure; no established security or loss-of-work consequence). Confidence: confirmed by source ordering analysis, not observed in execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Source and trigger: the sidebar and open view read independently (session_view.rs:913–920). A sidebar listing can have captured stale=true during the outage, while a newer session detail has already shown reachable Interrupted and admitted Restart. If that earlier sidebar HTTP reply lands after Restart success but before the view's Restart observation, list/view.rs:1985 calls retire_confirmed_restarts, session_ops.rs:77–79 treats stale=true as confirmation, and :215–226 clears restart_succeeded without checking the listing's start generation. ReadGate::accept_success (ops.rs:183–190) compares with the newest committed response, so an older request remains admissible until a newer listing commits; issuing the completion refresh does not fence it (list/view.rs:3417–3419, :2473–2474). The view observer at session_view.rs:549–564 sees the durable changed restart_revision but no successful flag, bumps generation without setting relaunched, and keep_terminal_surface (:3714–3722) still returns false for current Interrupted. Unlike a current detail that clears the flag, this old sidebar reply does not update the open view's current state. Contract: SPEC_impl.md:1136–1139 says 'Restart’s completion reattaches the agent terminal even after a refusal or lost reply. A view mounted during the request observes its completion, and one opened before the listing catches up can use the retained successful reply.' The assigned patch removes the listing-generation guard's test at old session_view.rs:4638–4649; the parent implementation had restart_listing_floor and required generation > floor (parent session_ops.rs:56–70, :107–109). Suggested correction: keep pre-reply listings from retiring the retained success, or preserve a durable successful-completion observation separately from retention. Material caveats: requires a delayed stale listing to land in the completion-to-effect window; normal post-completion detail refresh repairs it, so this does not establish a persistent outage or warrant high/highest by itself. A pre-reboot non-Interrupted listing can create the same ordering, but that is not needed for this source route. No reproductions or runtime tests run.

event.summary: A delayed pre-Restart stale listing can suppress terminal admission after success
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
After reconnecting to a host and successfully restarting an interrupted session, its already-open view can keep showing the interrupted recovery card until live detail arrives. A delayed sidebar response can erase the success before the view consumes it. The original temporary missing-terminal consequence is preserved; no permanent failure or destructive consequence is asserted.

## Details
Synthesis result: retain this source-supported conditional race, with the delivery-order premise explicit. It duplicates the caller-named g037/f3 and g038/l1 at this same full revision. Do not count these as three independently discovered defects. No parent drop is accepted or proposed. The earlier related g036/l1 at b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe has a distinct trigger/fix boundary, described below.

Complete trigger and source checks: aggregate.rs:547 captures host state before the awaited cached_slice at :578; row_of at :357 derives stale from that captured state. The in-flight sidebar can therefore carry stale=true from the earlier outage while the independent session detail has already reported nonstale Interrupted and enabled Restart. After the Restart POST succeeds, list/view.rs:3416–3419 records success, requests sidebar refresh and releases pending. No listing fence is inserted. The refresh calls reader::request_read (:644–680); SurfaceReader::claim/request (:405–458) explicitly leaves an existing running read alive and queues the new demand. ReadGate::accept_success (ops.rs:183–190) compares the reply generation with the latest applied listing, not Restart completion. Thus that old reply can still commit after pending release. list/view.rs:1985 calls retirement; session_ops.rs:77–80 treats stale as confirming regardless of status, and :215–226 clears restart_succeeded without a read-age floor.

Completion-to-effect ordering was independently checked in the pinned dependency source: Cargo.lock pins dioxus-core, dioxus-hooks and dioxus-desktop to 0.7.10. dioxus-hooks/src/use_effect.rs:15–47 queues a callback that reads shared state when it later runs. dioxus-core/src/virtual_dom.rs:507–537 polls ready tasks before effects and returns for dirty scopes; src/scheduler.rs:61–78 ranks effects below tasks and scopes. dioxus-desktop/src/webview.rs:537–590 returns while edits are unflushed before continuing virtual-DOM polling. These paths permit a ready old-list response task to retire success before the mounted completion observer; they do not guarantee that the observer wins. No actual task schedule was observed or reproduced.

The mounted view still owns its earlier nonstale Interrupted current; sidebar retirement does not replace that state. The selection bridge follows title and requests independent detail, rather than copying the sidebar status (session_view.rs:1245–1273). At :549–564 the observer sees the changed durable restart_revision and increments mount_generation, but with restart_succeeded cleared it cannot set relaunched=true. At :1709–1710 the desired set remains empty because terminal_absence/keep_terminal_surface (:3701–3722) rejects Interrupted with relaunched=false. This is lost terminal admission, not a lost numerical generation increment; preserving restart_revision alone does not settle it. The changed isolated observer test (:3915–3970) asserts the increment, not mounted terminal admission.

Repair and limits: connected GET session detail drains live supervisor sessions (sessions.rs:3052–3095 and :3195–3222); only its no-client branch (:3162–3192) serves cached metadata. Therefore the finding does not claim that a newly fetched connected detail inherits cached Interrupted through merged_status. The relevant old status is the mounted view's existing accepted detail. A successful post-Restart live detail repairs the gap. Detail failure may lengthen it but is not required to create the ordering. The precise unobserved runtime premise is delivery of the pre-completion stale sidebar reply after pending clears and before the mounted observer or fresh detail supplies the restarted run. Available source establishes that this is permitted, not its frequency. Runtime timing evidence would measure incidence, not supply a missing code path, and was not requested.

Cross-revision comparison: directly checked b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe session_ops.rs:50–114 and :188–233, plus session_view.rs:535–565 and :1252–1273. That revision already checks generation > restart_listing_floor, yet a newer eligible sidebar listing can clear Lifecycle.restart before the mounted observer uses it. Besides relaunched it can lose the reply terminal-kind override, an aspect absent after this group's grid-only change. Restoring the old floor or fencing pre-completion listing replies fixes this finding's specific stale-evidence trigger, but does not fix g036/l1's eligible-newer-listing consumer race. Keeping successful completion knowledge durable for mounted consumers separately from the retireable seed for future views could address both. Preserve these trigger and repair boundaries when deduplicating.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:1136–1139 says Restart completion reattaches the agent terminal, a view mounted during the request observes completion, and a view opened before the listing catches up can use the retained successful reply. SPEC.md Lifecycle operations:1897–1900 likewise preserves action outcomes across navigation and mounted completion observation. Suggested bucket: other, unchanged; temporary presentation/attachment failure only. Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. Confidence: likely, naming the response/effect ordering premise above; code paths and absence of ordering protection confirmed through source, behavior not observed in execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: duplicate g037/f3 and g038/l1 supplied by the caller; related but distinct g036/l1 as above. All earlier records remain preserved. No new discovery in this coverage-repair/synthesis turn. No open source lead, reproduction, test, build, or checkout change.

event.summary: Removing terminal kind and migration presentation matches the new attachment contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR considered: an old or restarting terminal might mount the wrong renderer after terminal-kind metadata and the migration band disappear. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: no, this concern establishes only unusable/misdrawn attachment, not a security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: the same revision mounts only the grid, removes byte-stream support at a protocol boundary, and ends legacy terminals before reload. Exact contract: SPEC_impl.md:3015–3019, 'Protocol 77 removed the byte streams with the old terminals and xterm.js: every attachment’s data channel carries a grid stream, so Attach, Attached and the browser’s socket say nothing about it, and SessionInfo and TabInfo no longer report a terminal kind.' SPEC_impl.md:2787–2788, 'This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host'. Source: terminal.js:3191–3221 gates on all grid scripts and the font, then mounts; :3387–3393 creates and fits the grid unconditionally before opening the socket. session_view.rs:1747–1778 retains encoded paths, attachment lease, generation and focus fields; no kind-dependent consumer remains in that path. Legacy remount-during-restart renderer selection and optimistic tab-kind tracking therefore serve no surviving contract. possible_cover: none. Caveats: protocol-skew compatibility is explicitly outside this conclusion; the same specification requires a reload for pages loaded before the helm update. No runtime execution.

event.summary: Replacing the tab-info projection preserves terminal identities and order
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Considered whether removing the richer tab projection could reorder tabs, change the selected shell, or move a terminal across the mount cap. Source comparison refutes that change in behavior.

## Details
The assigned patch replaces visible_tab_infos with visible_tabs at session_view.rs:1712, changes selection membership from comparing tab.id to ids.contains, and still takes the first MAX_MOUNTED_TAB_ISLANDS. In the parent revision, tabs.rs:198–216 implements visible_tab_infos by calling visible_tabs(server, opened, closed), then mapping each resulting id to Tab { id, kind } without changing order, count or identity. Its terminal.js:4686–4690 already directly constructs the grid for a host-kind terminal; :5247–5260 directly scrolls/flushes that grid on reveal, and :5475–5479 reveals a grid without the byte-write callback. Thus the callback claim was already false for the existing grid path before the first reviewed commit. Targeted git log -G 'term.write|reveal it performs' over the complete exclusive-base..inclusive-00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db range for session_view.rs returned no matching changes to that explanation. The assigned patch removes the other renderer and updates other terminology but introduces neither this prose nor the grid/callback mismatch. The continued high-level reason for JS ownership still applies; the inaccurate named mechanism is pre-range. No retired implementation was searched for independent runtime defects.

Suggested bucket: other, documentation accuracy, if addressed separately. Could-be-highest: no security or user-owned-work-loss route. This does not claim the comment is accurate. possible_cover: none in the supplied interface records. Original consequence preserved: future maintainers receive an obsolete lifecycle mechanism, without any established user-facing runtime failure. No tests, reproductions, builds or live-install actions. No remaining missing premise or open lead for l2.
